description: Built 31-10-2026 from the VATGER EDDK Tower SOP (Rev #14), the only operational source this session. Mode ids are runway-coded: single-runway '<rwy>AD' (EGCC's 05LAD pattern), dual '<rwy1><rwy2>AD' when both runways do both roles (no arr/dep role split stated, unlike LSZH/EGCC's segregated dual modes). 31RAD is primary (13L/31R 'primary for all arr/dep'); 13LAD its rare reciprocal. 31RAD31LAD models 13R/31L's 'high-demand periods' addition (not segregated, see research doc section 5). 31R24AD models 06/24's crosswind addition under the same 5kt tailwind cap; 06AD its rare reciprocal. Not built: a 13L-direction pairing (source ties additions only to 31-direction); a three-runway mode (ambiguous wording, two dual modes used instead of guessing). No maxCrosswindKt per mode. No minima/approachLadder/capacity, matching LSZH/EGCC -- two non-precision visibility minima (13R >=2.1km, 24 >=1.5km) are in the research doc only. Full detail: docs/EDDK_RUNWAY_RESEARCH.md.

modes.description: Single-runway default, westerly: 31R arrivals and departures. Primary mode (VATGER: 13L/31R 'primary for all arrivals/departures'); preferred up to 5kt tailwind (settings.json tailwindDryKt).
Single-runway default, easterly: 13L arrivals and departures. Rare reciprocal of 31RAD, used when the tailwind component on 31R would exceed 5kt.

Dual, high-demand westerly: 31R and 31L both handle arrivals and departures. Models VATGER's '13R/31L...usable for light/medium traffic in high-demand periods' statement. Not segregated -- the source gives no arrival/departure role split for this pair, unlike LSZH/EGCC's segregated dual modes.

Primary plus crosswind-runway capacity boost, westerly: 31R and 24 both handle arrivals and departures. Models VATGER's 'ops via 31R/31L direction (and 24, also capped at 5kt tailwind)' -- 24 activated under the same tailwind condition as the 31-direction preference.

Rare crosswind-only mode, easterly: 06 arrivals and departures. Reciprocal of 31R24AD's 24 leg; VATGER states direction 06 is 'used very rarely' since the prevailing wind in Cologne Bay is north/northwest.
